issuer: the Government of Nunavut (the Registrar under the Traffic Safety Act)
note: Read 2026-11-03 in the Government of Nunavut's legislation site (nunavutlegislation.ca), in the PDFs saved that day (its pages answer this client with a Cloudflare challenge). Age: 16. The Driver's Licence Regulations (R.R.N.W.T. 1990,c.M-27), s. 3(2): the Registrar shall not issue a Class 5 or 6 licence to anyone under sixteen; s. 3(3): a Class 7 from fifteen, which R-042-2018, s. 3.1, makes the learner's licence. They were read in the office consolidation as amended to R-042-98, which says it isn't an official statement of the law; the two later amendments read, R-042-2018 and R-041-2021, don't touch s. 3, and whether another amendment since 1998 does wasn't found. No stage between the learner's Class 7 and the Class 5 is in what was read, so the full licence is held from sixteen. Term and fee: R-041-2021 (registered 23 September 2021), s. 8: a licence expires on its holder's birthday in the fifth year after the end of the year it's issued, or, if a holder who is an adult chooses it when it's issued, in the tenth; Schedule E, item 1: $70 for a 5-year term, $140 for a 10-year; item 9: half the fee from sixty. So four terms are held: five years at $70 and ten at $140 from nineteen (an adult: Nunavut's age of majority, as the ages engine holds it), each under sixty; from sixty, five years at $35 and ten at $70. A term runs to a birthday, so its years are held as five and ten. The Class 5 examination ($30, item 2(c)) isn't held. The general identification card wasn't found in any text read, so none is held.

sources.title: Consolidation of Driver's Licence Regulations, R.R.N.W.T. 1990,c.M-27, as amended to R-042-98 (Nunavut office consolidation, bilingual; not an official statement of the law)
sources.said: 3. (1) The Registrar shall not issue a Class 1, 2, 3 or 4 driver's licence to a person unless that person is at least 18 years of age. (2) The Registrar shall not issue a Class 5 or 6 driver's licence to a person unless that person is at least 16 years of age. (3) The Registrar shall not issue a Class 7 driver's licence to a person unless that person is at least 15 years of age. R-052-94,s.3.

sources.title: Driver's Licence Regulations, amendment, R-042-2018 (Motor Vehicles Act), registered 2018-12-06, Government of Nunavut
sources.said: 3.1. A Class 7 driver's licence is categorized as a learner's driver's licence for the purposes of the Act.

sources.title: Driver's Licence Regulations, amendment, R-041-2021 (Traffic Safety Act), registered 2021-09-23, Government of Nunavut
sources.said: 8. (1) Subject to subsection (2), a driver's licence expires on the birthday of the license holder in the fifth year after the end of the year in which the licence is issued. (2) A driver's licence expires on the birthday of the license holder in the tenth year after the end of the year in which the licence is issued if (a) the licence holder choses this option at the time the driver's licence is issued; and (b) the licence holder is an adult at the time the driver's licence is issued. ... SCHEDULE E ... 1. All classes of driver's licence (a) issued for a 5 year term $70 (b) issued for a 10 year term $140 ... 9. Despite items 1 to 4, the fee payable by a person who has attained 60 years of age or more is (a) for a driver's licence 50% of the applicable fee set out in item 1
